submission.natural_language_explanation: Duplicate-token head whose attention on a word's first occurrence is drained by every earlier 'sink' token in the text (commas, periods, line breaks, '(' and the words the/a/an/in/for/to/on/of/and): a word or name fires on first occurrence only when at most one sink precedes it after the text's first token ('Gerda Gilboe', 'Then we saw Sandusky', 'My uncle told me that he met Hartley'; names stay active after one sink, at about 0.25-0.5 of max), and once three or more sinks precede it only a token with an earlier copy in the text fires: the second or later copy of a capitalised name or rare word/code piece (' Hart' in 'roads to Hartlepool ... letters from Hartlepool', ' Prec', 'Value' in 'getValue ... setValue'), strongest on long-range repeats and third copies. Predict inactive any text whose first content word (after its first token) comes after at least two sinks ('Then, in the ...', 'It was in the ...', 'So, in the ...') and in which no capitalised name or rare piece occurs twice; first-occurrence names, numbers, punctuation runs and function words there stay inactive (the one known exception is ' Ger' of Gerlach), while a common lowercase word repeated in such a text, or a content word after exactly one sink ('In the office nobody wanted'), is unreliable and not claimed either way.

rival_explanations: Position-only: first occurrences fire within roughly the first eight tokens of any text whatever precedes them and never later, so 'Then, the Sandusky play' (two sinks, token 3) is active and 'My uncle told me that he met Hartley' (no sinks, token 7) is borderline, unlike the sink-count reading.

Broader repeat reading: the second copy of any content word fires, so repeated common nouns ('the bell rang ... rang the bell', 'a jar of jam, a jar of honey') are reliably active in sink-heavy text, not just repeated names and rare pieces.

Narrower: only capitalised proper-name pieces fire (first occurrence early, or as repeats), so repeated lowercase code or foreign fragments ('getValue ... setValue', 'samplingProfiler ... samplingProfiler') stay inactive.
